option_description: Whether the agent encrypts its egress telemetry channel (logs/metrics/syslog) to the backend with TLS, rather than forwarding over plaintext TCP/UDP.
security_impact: References "Cleartext telemetry forwarding (sniffing / MITM)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false (cleartext forward). Plaintext forwarding exposes the telemetry payload and any embedded backend credentials to passive sniffing and active MITM/injection on the path.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Fluentd forward output for a TLS transport block
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A <transport tls> block with cert_path/private_key_path inside the <source>/<match> forward block (secure), or a forward source/match with NO transport tls (insecure cleartext).
how_to_obtain.source: Fluentd forward input plugin (security & transport tls)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Filebeat output for https:// hosts and an ssl block
how_to_obtain.expected_output: output.elasticsearch.hosts use https:// and ssl.* keys present (secure); http:// hosts or no ssl block (insecure).

option_description: Whether the agent validates the backend server's TLS certificate rather than accepting any certificate (verification_mode: none / Fluentd insecure true).
security_impact: References "Cleartext telemetry forwarding (sniffing / MITM)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. Disabling certificate validation accepts any cert, re-enabling MITM despite 'TLS on' — a control bypass of encryption_in_transit_enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Filebeat ssl.verification_mode and any Fluentd insecure flag
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl.verification_mode: full or key absent (default full = secure); ssl.verification_mode: none (insecure). Default is full.

option_description: Minimum negotiated TLS version on the agent's egress/endpoints (Filebeat ssl.supported_protocols, Fluentd transport tls, exporter-toolkit tls_server_config.min_version).
security_impact: References "Cleartext telemetry forwarding (sniffing / MITM)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when the floor is in [TLS1.0, TLS1.1, SSLv3]. A downgraded floor exposes telemetry to known protocol-downgrade weaknesses even when encryption is nominally on; NIST SP 800-52r2 floor is TLS 1.2.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the configured minimum TLS version on the exporter/agent endpoints
how_to_obtain.expected_output: min_version: TLS12 or TLS13 (secure); TLS10/TLS11 (insecure). Exporter-toolkit default baseline is TLS 1.2+.
how_to_obtain.source: Prometheus exporter-toolkit web configuration (TLS, basic auth, client_auth_type)

option_description: Whether the agent's HTTP scrape/forward listening endpoint requires authentication. node_exporter serves /metrics with NO auth unless --web.config.file sets basic_auth_users/client cert; Fluentd in_forward without <security> is open.
security_impact: References "Unauthenticated agent listening endpoint exposure" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. An unauthenticated scrape/forward listener leaks host inventory, mount points, and process/network stats to any reaching peer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether node_exporter was started with a web.config.file and whether /metrics answers without auth
how_to_obtain.command: ps -ef | grep node_exporter | grep -oE 'web.config(.file)?=[^ ]+'; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:9100/metrics
how_to_obtain.expected_output: web.config.file flag present pointing at a YAML with basic_auth_users/tls_server_config (secure); flag absent and curl returns 200 with no auth (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Prometheus exporter-toolkit web configuration (TLS, basic auth, client_auth_type)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the exporter web-config defines basic auth users or required client cert
how_to_obtain.expected_output: basic_auth_users populated and/or client_auth_type: RequireAndVerifyClientCert with client_ca_file (secure mTLS). Other client_auth_type values are documented as insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: Prometheus exporter-toolkit web configuration (TLS, basic auth, client_auth_type)

option_description: Whether the agent's listening endpoint is bound to loopback (127.0.0.1) or a restricted internal interface behind a TLS proxy/firewall, rather than 0.0.0.0 / :: (all interfaces).
security_impact: References "Unauthenticated agent listening endpoint exposure" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false (world/network-reachable bind). A non-loopback bind on an unauthenticated endpoint exposes the scrape/forward surface to the network.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the listen address from the running agent and confirm the bound interface with ss
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Listen address 127.0.0.1 (secure) vs 0.0.0.0 / :: (insecure). ss shows whether the metrics/forward port is bound to a public interface.
how_to_obtain.source: Prometheus exporter-toolkit web configuration (TLS, basic auth, client_auth_type)

option_description: Whether the agent's scrape/metrics/forward endpoint is reachable from the public internet (public IP bind with no firewall/security-group restriction), not merely on all local interfaces.
security_impact: References "Unauthenticated agent listening endpoint exposure" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is true. A world-reachable unauthenticated /metrics leaks host inventory and presents attack surface such as an exposed embedded HTTP server.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an external network position, attempt to reach the metrics/forward port to determine public reachability
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection refused/timeout from the internet (secure, not internet-reachable); HTTP 200 metrics body returned from outside (insecure, internet-reachable).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the host's firewall / cloud security-group rules for the metrics/forward port against the public IP bind
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Port restricted to a private CIDR / management subnet (secure); open 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on a public IP (internet-reachable).

option_description: Whether the agent proves its own identity to the SIEM/log backend on egress (Fluentd <security> shared_key + user_auth; Filebeat api_key, username/password, or PKI client cert).
security_impact: References "Weak / missing agent-to-backend authentication" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. Server-only TLS authenticates the backend but not the agent, so a rogue forwarder can inject telemetry and a stolen channel can be replayed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Fluentd forward config for a <security> block with shared_key/user_auth
how_to_obtain.expected_output: <security> block with self_hostname and shared_key (secure). Absence of <security>, or allow_anonymous_source true, means unauthenticated forwarding (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Fluentd forward input plugin (security & transport tls)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Filebeat output for a backend credential
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An api_key, username/password, or ssl.certificate (PKI) under output.* (secure); none present (insecure).

option_description: Whether the agent's forward receiver accepts telemetry from unauthenticated/anonymous sources (Fluentd allow_anonymous_source, which DEFAULTS true when no <security> block is present).
security_impact: References "Weak / missing agent-to-backend authentication" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is true. Any network peer can then push records into the pipeline with no client identity.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Fluentd in_forward receiver for allow_anonymous_source and a <security> block
how_to_obtain.expected_output: <security> block present with shared_key and allow_anonymous_source false (secure); no <security> block / allow_anonymous_source true (default — anonymous sources accepted, insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Fluentd forward input plugin (security & transport tls)

option_description: Whether mutual TLS is in effect so the agent presents a client certificate the backend verifies against a truststore (Fluentd client_cert_auth + ca_path; Filebeat ssl.certificate + ssl.key).
security_impact: References "Weak / missing agent-to-backend authentication" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false (server-side TLS only, no client-cert auth). mTLS authenticates the agent by certificate rather than only a shared secret.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for client-certificate auth on the egress channel (Fluentd client_cert_auth/ca_path, Filebeat ssl.certificate/ssl.key)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: client_cert_auth true + ca_path (Fluentd) or ssl.certificate/ssl.key (Filebeat) present = mTLS (secure); absent = no client-cert auth.
how_to_obtain.source: Fluentd forward input plugin (security & transport tls)

option_description: Supporting context: whether the backend shared_key/api_key/password the agent presents is a keystore/env (${VAR}) reference on a 0600 root-owned config rather than inline plaintext in a world-readable config.
security_impact: Supporting context for "Weak / missing agent-to-backend authentication" — not itself the trigger. A credential that authenticates the agent but is trivially readable locally weakens the authentication guarantee.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check config permissions/ownership and whether the backend credential is a literal or a ${VAR}/keystore reference
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode 600/640 owned by root (secure); 644+ or other-readable with inline cleartext secret (insecure). Values referencing ${ENV} or keystore rather than literals are secure.

option_description: Effective SNMP version and SNMPv3 security level the agent's snmpd exposes (net-snmp /etc/snmp/snmpd.conf): v1/v2c cleartext community vs SNMPv3 noauth/authnopriv/authpriv.
security_impact: References "SNMP cleartext community-string read/write (v1/v2c)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is in {v1, v2c, v3_noauth, v3_authnopriv}. v1/v2c authenticate with a cleartext community string trivially sniffed on an adjacent segment; v3 below authPriv leaves the polled MIB payload unencrypted in transit. Only v3_authpriv or disabled is secure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the community and v3 user lines from snmpd.conf to derive version/security level
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only createUser + rouser/rwuser ... priv lines (secure SNMPv3 authPriv); any rocommunity/rwcommunity line = cleartext v1/v2c community (insecure). Default-named 'public'/'private' communities are an immediate finding.
how_to_obtain.source: net-snmp snmpd.conf man page (rocommunity/rwcommunity, createUser, rouser/rwuser)

how_to_obtain.instruction: For SNMPv3, confirm the per-user security level is priv (authPriv)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: rouser <user> priv (secure); rouser <user> noauth / auth (insecure). net-snmp requires OpenSSL support for SHA auth and AES privacy.
how_to_obtain.source: net-snmp snmpd.conf man page (rocommunity/rwcommunity, createUser, rouser/rwuser)

option_description: Whether any rocommunity/rwcommunity line uses a well-known default community string (public/private) — an immediate guess-without-sniffing finding.
security_impact: References "SNMP cleartext community-string read/write (v1/v2c)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is true. A default community is guessable without even sniffing, granting MIB read (rocommunity) or device write (rwcommunity).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the rocommunity/rwcommunity tokens and check for default values
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No community lines / non-default token (secure); 'public' or 'private' token present (default community in use — insecure, immediate finding).
how_to_obtain.source: net-snmp snmpd.conf man page (rocommunity/rwcommunity, createUser, rouser/rwuser)

option_description: Whether backend authentication secrets (Fluentd shared_key, Filebeat api_key/password, Promtail/Loki bearer tokens) are written as inline plaintext literals in the agent config rather than referenced via keystore or ${ENV}.
security_impact: References "Plaintext backend credentials in agent config" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is true. Any local reader of the config obtains credentials to write to or impersonate the SIEM/log backend.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the agent config for secret keys and inspect whether values are literals or ${VAR}/keystore references; also read perms
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode 600/640 owned by root (secure); 644+ or other-readable with inline cleartext secret (insecure). Values referencing ${ENV} or keystore rather than literals are secure.

option_description: Whether the agent resolves backend secrets through an external secret store (Filebeat keystore, ${VAR} env indirection, or an injected-at-runtime mechanism) rather than embedding them in config.
security_impact: References "Plaintext backend credentials in agent config" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. When secrets are not externalized (combined with unhardened config permissions), inline secrets are exposed to any local reader.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm secrets resolve via keystore/env rather than appearing as literals in config
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secret keys appear as ${VAR}/keystore references and keystore list shows the keys (externalized — secure); raw literal token/password values inline (not externalized — insecure).

option_description: Whether the agent config file (and any readable spooled buffer/registry that may carry secrets) is root-owned with restrictive mode (0600/0640) and not world/group-readable.
security_impact: References "Plaintext backend credentials in agent config" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. A world-readable config (0644/0666) exposes any inline credentials to local readers.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run stat on the agent config and any secret-bearing spool/registry
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode 600/640 owned by root, and buffer/registry dirs 700/600 owned by the agent user (secure); 644+ or world/group-readable (insecure).

option_description: Whether the agent process runs as a dedicated unprivileged user with need-based scoping (adm group, file ACLs, or Linux capabilities for log read) rather than root (uid 0).
security_impact: References "Agent-root host privilege escalation" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false (agent runs as root). A root-context agent turns any agent RCE/parser bug or host local-privesc into full host compromise; least privilege shrinks blast radius.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the effective process user for the running agent
how_to_obtain.command: ps -o user= -C node_exporter,fluentd,filebeat,vector,promtail 2>/dev/null; systemctl show fluentd filebeat -p User 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A dedicated non-root user (secure); 'root' / empty (defaults to root) for the agent process (insecure — broadens blast radius of any agent CVE).

option_description: Whether the host and agent are current on security patches for known local-privesc and agent CVEs — notably sudo > 1.9.5p1 (CVE-2021-3156 Baron Samedit) and a patched agent build (e.g. Fluent Bit >= 3.0.4 / 2.2.3 for CVE-2024-4323).
security_impact: References "Agent-root host privilege escalation" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. An unpatched local-root primitive (e.g. sudo Baron Samedit) is amplified by a root-context agent into full host compromise.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check sudo and agent versions against their CVE fix lines
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Fluent Bit >= 3.0.4 / 2.2.3 (patched for CVE-2024-4323); sudo > 1.9.5p1 (patched for CVE-2021-3156). Lower versions = exposed.
how_to_obtain.source: Fluent Bit CVE-2024-4323 advisory / NVD CVE-2021-3156

option_description: Raw effective OS user the agent process runs under (e.g. 'root', 'fluent', 'filebeat'); context for deriving the least-privilege boolean.
security_impact: Derivation input for "Agent-root host privilege escalation" — feeds agent_runs_as_non_root_least_privilege rather than triggering directly. 'root' or empty (systemd default) indicates uid 0.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the effective process user for the agent
how_to_obtain.command: ps -o user= -C node_exporter,fluentd,filebeat,vector,promtail 2>/dev/null; systemctl show fluentd filebeat -p User 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The username string under which the agent runs (e.g. 'fluent', 'filebeat', or 'root'/empty indicating uid 0).

option_description: Whether the agent build is patched against publicly-known critical CVEs in its parsers / embedded HTTP server — the triggering case is CVE-2024-4323 (Fluent Bit 2.0.7-3.0.3, CVSS 9.8) in the /api/v1/traces parser.
security_impact: References "Agent parser / embedded-HTTP RCE (patch currency)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false (unpatched exploitable build). The memory-corruption enables DoS, info disclosure, and potentially RCE; fixed in Fluent Bit 3.0.4 / 2.2.3.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare the agent version against the vendor CVE fix floor
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Fluent Bit >= 3.0.4 (or backported 2.2.3) = patched for CVE-2024-4323 (secure); 2.0.7-3.0.3 = unpatched exploitable build (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Fluent Bit CVE-2024-4323 advisory / NVD CVE-2021-3156

option_description: Whether the running agent version is a vendor-supported (non-EOL) release that still receives security backports.
security_impact: Supporting context for "Agent parser / embedded-HTTP RCE (patch currency)" — not itself a trigger. An EOL build cannot receive the CVE-2024-4323 fix and compounds patch-currency exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running agent version, then compare against the vendor supported-release/EOL matrix
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version string maps to a vendor-supported (non-EOL) release receiving security backports (secure); a release past EOL on the vendor matrix (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: Fluent Bit CVE-2024-4323 advisory / NVD CVE-2021-3156

option_description: Whether the agent's embedded HTTP / monitoring server (the attack surface for CVE-2024-4323's /api/v1/traces parser) is disabled or bound only to loopback rather than network-reachable.
security_impact: References "Agent parser / embedded-HTTP RCE (patch currency)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false (HTTP server enabled and bound to a non-loopback/world-reachable address). Disabling it or loopback-binding keeps the vulnerable parser unreachable by a network peer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Fluent Bit embedded HTTP server config and confirm the listen interface
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP_Server Off or bound to loopback (reduces CVE-2024-4323 exposure); HTTP_Server On listening on 0.0.0.0 with a vulnerable version = exploitable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the embedded HTTP port's bound interface on the wire
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No listener, or listener bound to 127.0.0.1 (secure); bound to 0.0.0.0/:: (network-reachable, insecure).

option_description: Whether the agent's reachable embedded HTTP / monitoring endpoint requires authentication (or sits behind an authenticating reverse proxy / network ACL) before the parser processes a request.
security_impact: References "Agent parser / embedded-HTTP RCE (patch currency)" — one of its conditions (AND-combined with embedded_http_server_disabled_or_loopback being insecure), firing when this is false. An unauthenticated reachable endpoint makes the CVE-2024-4323 parser directly exploitable by any network peer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the embedded HTTP endpoint to see whether it answers without credentials
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 401/403 or no response (authenticated / behind ACL — secure); 200 returned with no credential challenge (unauthenticated — insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm whether an authenticating reverse proxy or network ACL fronts the embedded HTTP endpoint
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An auth proxy / restrictive firewall ACL is documented in front of the endpoint (secure); the endpoint is reachable directly with no auth layer (insecure).

option_description: Whether the agent masks/scrubs sensitive data (credentials, tokens, PII/PHI) before forwarding telemetry (Fluentd record_modifier/grep/scrub/gsub, Vector remap/redact, Filebeat processors drop_fields).
security_impact: References "Sensitive-data / PII over-collection (no masking)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. Forwarding raw telemetry verbatim over-collects secrets and personal data into the monitoring tier (NIST SP 800-122 data minimization).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the agent pipeline for masking/scrub/drop stages
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of a masking/redaction/drop filter in the pipeline (secure data minimization); none = raw forwarding of potentially sensitive payloads (insecure).

option_description: Whether explicit scrub/redact/drop_fields filters are configured in the agent pipeline to remove PII/PHI and secret patterns prior to egress.
security_impact: References "Sensitive-data / PII over-collection (no masking)" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. With no redaction filter, credentials and personal data reach the backend in full, creating data-residency/retention liabilities for anyone with SIEM access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm explicit scrub/redact/drop_fields filters targeting sensitive patterns exist in the pipeline
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more redaction/drop filters targeting PII/secret fields present (secure); no such filter (insecure).

option_description: Contextual evidence: whether a data-minimization posture (collect/forward only what is operationally required) is enforced for the agent's telemetry per NIST SP 800-122.
security_impact: Supporting context for "Sensitive-data / PII over-collection (no masking)" — supports interpretation of the masking/redaction triggers but is not itself a firing condition.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a documented/enforced collect-only-what-is-needed posture for the agent's telemetry per NIST SP 800-122
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented data-minimization policy with a scoped input/field selection enforced in the pipeline (secure); broad raw collection with no minimization rationale (weak context).

option_description: Whether the agent config files AND their containing directories are writable only by root/admin (owned root, not group/other-writable; files <=0644, dirs 0755 root).
security_impact: References "Agent config tamper / SIEM blinding" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false (config writable by non-admin). A non-admin attacker could disable forwarding (blind the SIEM), redirect telemetry to an attacker sink, or inject an exec/parser stage that runs as the agent's (often root) user.

how_to_obtain.instruction: stat the agent config files and parent dirs, and find any non-admin-writable agent config
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Config owned root:root and NOT other/group-writable (secure); any agent config writable by non-admin = tamper risk (insecure).

option_description: Whether any remote/local config-reload or admin/monitoring HTTP endpoint exposed by the agent requires authentication.
security_impact: References "Agent config tamper / SIEM blinding" — one of its OR-conditions, firing when this is false. An unauthenticated reload/admin endpoint lets an attacker hot-swap pipeline config or trigger a reload of attacker-planted config without credentials — the same SIEM-blinding/telemetry-redirect tamper without filesystem write.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the agent for an embedded HTTP/admin/reload endpoint and whether it is auth-gated
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No reload/admin endpoint exposed, or one fronted by auth/ACL (secure); an enabled HTTP admin/reload endpoint with no auth (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the reload/admin endpoint for an unauthenticated response
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 401/403/connection refused (authenticated or absent — secure); 200 without a credential challenge (unauthenticated reload/admin surface — insecure).

option_description: Whether changes to the agent config or a stop/disable of telemetry forwarding are detected (FIM/config-integrity monitoring on the agent config, heartbeat or dead-man's-switch alerting on forwarding cessation at the SIEM).
security_impact: References "Agent config tamper / SIEM blinding" — one of its OR-conditions (secondary), firing when this is false. With no tamper/cessation monitoring, an attacker who edits the config or kills forwarding blinds the SIEM silently during the intrusion window.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm FIM/config-integrity monitoring on the agent config and SIEM-side heartbeat/dead-man's-switch alerting on forwarding cessation
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A FIM rule covers the agent config path and the SIEM alerts on missing heartbeats from the agent (secure); neither tamper nor cessation is detected (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the SIEM raised an alert during a controlled forwarding-stop test (stop the agent and confirm a cessation alert fires)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A dead-man's-switch / missing-heartbeat alert is recorded when forwarding stops (monitored — secure); no alert generated (unmonitored — insecure).
